brief.greeting: Good morning. Your overnight feed includes a router that learns to cut costs and a systemd that finally speaks Rust.

stories.headline: EvoRouter trims cost for multi-agent routing
stories.body: **Self‑evolving routing framework:** EvoRouter blends expert cost feedback with token‑level supervision to prune routes on the fly, cutting compute without hurting performance.
stories.why: Engineers can run cheaper multi‑agent pipelines with predictable latency.

stories.headline: FOCUS sharpens long‑horizon LM critics
stories.body: **Active branch selection:** FOCUS lets the critic train on carefully chosen trajectory forks, slashing estimation error for language‑model agents that plan far ahead.
stories.why: More reliable planning lets your LLM agents handle complex tasks with fewer surprises.

stories.headline: systemd to host Rust leaf components
stories.body: **Optional Rust modules:** systemd v263 will allow leaf services written in Rust, giving you memory‑safe plugins without rewriting the whole init system.
stories.why: You can add safe extensions to the core of Linux without a full migration.

quick_hits.text: **Eurogame arena:** DECE runs 1,032 LLM matches across ten board games.
**Code security boost:** GPT‑6.1 Sol powers CodeRabbit’s scan of complex codebases.
**Offline AI:** Hob lets you run Claude‑style models locally on all major OSes.
**IPO filing:** Anthropic submits S‑1 to the SEC for a public offering.
**Security patches:** LWN reports updates for AlmaLinux, Debian, and Fedora packages.

brief.sign_off: Catch you tomorrow, and keep hacking.

highlights.title: EvoRouter: Cost-Efficient Multi-Agent Routing via Insight-Guided On-Policy Distillation
highlights.summary: EvoRouter is a self-evolving multi-agent routing framework that uses insight‑guided on‑policy distillation to combine expert‑derived performance‑cost feedback with dense token‑level supervision.
highlights.detail: The system periodically synthesizes conditional routing insights about capability needs, resource scaling returns, and configuration interactions, then feeds them to a privileged teacher that guides the router's planning. This addresses the combinatorial explosion of configuration space and sparse reward signals in large‑scale web query serving.

related.title: The Thin Orchestrator: How We Made Our AI Agents More Reliable by Giving the Router Less to Do

highlights.title: FOCUS: Active Critic Learning for Long-Horizon Language Model Agents
highlights.summary: FOCUS is an RL method that actively selects trajectory branches to train a critic network, reducing estimation error for long‑horizon language‑model agents.
highlights.detail: By sampling continuations from states expected to most improve the critic, FOCUS provides targeted training targets and uses TD(λ) advantages to score state segments. This mitigates the high cost of exhaustive continuation sampling while improving credit assignment for sparse outcome rewards.

related.title: ReFlow: Replay-Driven Decoupling for Efficient RL Post-Training

highlights.title: A Unified Arena for LLM Agents across Diverse Eurogame
highlights.summary: DECE offers a unified arena covering ten Eurogames to evaluate LLM agents across diverse competitive settings, running 1,032 matches in total.
highlights.detail: The study tested 12 model‑harness configurations spanning nine models and four execution harnesses, providing cross‑game performance insights. Shared interfaces and protocols enable systematic comparison of strategic commitments, resource competition, and multiple victory routes.

highlights.title: ESP32 Rotary Display Makes Ideal Timer
highlights.summary: Hackaday featured an ESP32‑based rotary display that functions as a precise timer.
highlights.detail: The project repurposes the ESP32 microcontroller with a rotary encoder and OLED screen to create a compact, programmable timer. It demonstrates how low‑cost embedded hardware can be adapted for niche utility tasks.

highlights.title: Concerning behavior from a popular open-weight AI model
highlights.summary: A Hacker News discussion flagged concerning behavior from a widely used open‑weight AI model.
highlights.detail: The post highlighted unexpected or unsafe outputs observed in the model, prompting community scrutiny and calls for further safety evaluation.

items.title: GPT-6.1 Sol helps CodeRabbit strengthen security across complex codebases
items.summary: CodeRabbit integrates GPT‑6.1 Sol to scan complex codebases for security risks and assist developers with review and remediation.
items.detail: The GPT‑6.1 Sol security agent generates findings and suggested fixes, aiming to streamline vulnerability detection in large software projects. This represents a new release of OpenAI's model applied to code security.

items.title: Show HN: Hob - Open-source, on device alternative to Claude Cowork and ChatGPT
items.summary: Hob is an MIT‑licensed desktop app that runs open‑weight models locally on Mac, Windows, and Linux, providing offline Claude/ChatGPT‑style functionality.
items.detail: The app automatically selects the best open‑weight model for the hardware, supports sandboxed Python code generation, web search via SearXNG, and local file system CRUD, keeping all data on the device unless the user enables online features.

items.title: Anthropic files S-1 with the SEC for proposed initial public offering
items.summary: Anthropic filed an S‑1 registration statement with the SEC to begin a proposed initial public offering.
items.detail: The filing signals Anthropic's intention to go public, moving from private funding to a public market. It includes financial disclosures and outlines the company's business, but no valuation or pricing details were disclosed.

items.title: ChatGPT’s expanding world of work
items.summary: OpenAI’s Signals data shows ChatGPT is used for 165 distinct work activities in almost 100 countries.
items.detail: The analysis tracks how professionals integrate ChatGPT into daily tasks, revealing regional adoption patterns and shifts in usage over time. It highlights growing reliance on AI assistants across diverse industries without claiming performance improvements.

related.title: How we built ChatGPT’s novel ad stack for user trust and relevance

items.title: Greptile takes bug detection beyond code review with GPT-6 Astra
items.summary: Greptile announced a workflow‑testing platform that leverages GPT‑6 Astra, Daybreak security tooling, and Codex for code rework reduction.
items.detail: The service extends beyond traditional code review by simulating user interactions and automatically identifying bugs. Daybreak adds a security layer, while Codex helps developers refactor code, aiming to cut development cycles.

items.title: Meta Networking at the 2026 OCP Global Summit: Open Innovation for Scale-Up, Scale-Out, and Scale-Across AI Networks
items.summary: Meta unveiled a liquid‑cooled network rack at the 2026 OCP Global Summit featuring 102.4 Tbps of switch capacity using 128 × 800 Gbps blades.
items.detail: The rack, named IcePack & IceCube, uses Broadcom Tomahawk 6C and NVIDIA Spectrum‑6 ASICs to support Meta’s Muse Wonder, Muse Spark, and the gigawatt‑scale Prometheus AI cluster. It targets both scale‑up and scale‑out AI workloads.

related.title: OCP Summit 2026: Powering AI with Open Innovations in Scale-Up, Scale-Out, and Scale-Across Networks

items.title: Security updates for Monday
items.summary: LWN reported a batch of security updates for AlmaLinux, Debian, and Fedora covering dozens of packages.
items.detail: Updates address vulnerabilities in components such as OpenSSL, kernel, Node.js, and PostgreSQL pgvector across multiple distributions. Administrators are urged to apply the patches promptly to maintain system integrity.

items.title: Systemd adds support for components written in Rust
items.summary: Systemd will include optional leaf component support written in Rust starting with the v263 release expected in December.
items.detail: Only new leaf components can be implemented in Rust; existing code remains unchanged and no dependent components are rewritten. The Rust integration is limited by dynamic library support, which could increase binary sizes if fully adopted.

items.title: Two stable kernels for Monday
items.summary: Linux stable kernels 7.2.13 and 6.18.59 have been released, containing numerous fixes.
items.detail: Both kernels are part of the regular maintenance series and are recommended for users to upgrade to benefit from the accumulated patches across the tree.

related.title: Seven stable kernels for Thursday with fix for critical vulnerability

items.title: [$] Python's experimental JIT to be removed
items.summary: Python's experimental JIT added for the 3.13 release in 2024 is being discontinued after the withdrawal of PEP 836.
items.detail: The steering council paused JIT development pending a formal PEP with clear maintenance and compatibility criteria; without it, the JIT maintainers halted work, effectively ending the project for now.

items.title: Arduino Engine Runs Many Games
items.summary: An Arduino Uno has been used to run a port of the ZX Spectrum game Manic Miner, demonstrating the platform's ability to host classic games despite limited memory.
items.detail: The project, led by Smashcat, required careful memory optimization to fit the game within the Uno's constraints, showcasing Arduino's potential for retro gaming applications.

items.title: Priority-Aware Scheduler for Serverless Functions Provision and Load Balancing
items.summary: SPES-Ext is a rule‑based priority‑aware scheduler for serverless functions that targets memory‑constrained distributed workers.
items.detail: It leverages observed concentration in invocation patterns to predict behavior, aiming to reduce cold‑start latency while balancing resource usage, addressing shortcomings of existing preloading strategies.

items.title: Connecting Quantum Proof Systems and Hoare Logic
items.summary: The Qafny quantum proof system can be fully translated into classical Hoare logic with array theory, enabling verification of quantum programs using existing tools.
items.detail: The translation is sound and complete; every Qafny proof becomes a valid Hoare triple, and the authors mechanized the completeness direction in Rocq, lowering the barrier to quantum software verification.

related.title: QEDIA: Quantum Program Verification in Lean

items.title: A Unified Queueing-Based Framework for Comparative Evaluation of Serverless Autoscaling Strategies under Bursty Workloads
items.summary: A unified queueing-network and queueing Petri net framework models three serverless autoscaling strategies—SPR, CLS, and MBS—to compare their QoS performance under bursty workloads.
items.detail: The framework abstracts away proprietary platform details, enabling systematic evaluation of scaling behavior. It combines analytical queueing theory with a Java implementation of QPNs, allowing researchers to simulate workload spikes and SLA compliance across strategies.

items.title: Cross-Domain Sequential Recommendation with Representation-Level User Transfer
items.summary: A cross-domain sequential recommendation system transfers user representations via a lightweight adapter, avoiding sharing raw interaction data or item embeddings between source and target domains.
items.detail: The approach addresses business constraints that isolate data and handles users lacking cross-domain activity. By projecting source-domain user vectors into the target embedding space, it integrates seamlessly with the target interaction sequence, simplifying deployment in privacy-sensitive settings.

items.title: ACTIVE: A Dynamic Pareto-Frontier-Based Unified Index for Dual-Vector Query
items.summary: ACTIVE introduces a dynamic Pareto-frontier index for dual-vector queries that supports fast construction, updates, and high retrieval quality across varying attribute weightings.
items.detail: Existing dual-vector ANNS methods struggle with inefficiencies in building and maintaining the index. ACTIVE mitigates these issues while preserving performance, making Pareto-frontier‑based retrieval practical for applications where entities have multiple vector representations.

items.title: Accelerating SO(2)-Equivariant Materials Models through Low-Precision Emulation
items.summary: FlashSO(2) accelerates SO(2)-equivariant GNN layers using emulated low‑precision integer operations, achieving up to 30× speedup on NVIDIA Hopper and 60× on Blackwell GPUs.
items.detail: The method replaces FP32 tensor ops with integer‑based Ozaki scheme emulation, preserving model accuracy while exploiting FP8‑class hardware. It targets the dominant runtime layers of state‑of‑the‑art ML interatomic potentials and universal Hamiltonian models.

items.title: HarnessRouter/harnessrouter
items.summary: HarnessRouter Community Edition is a self‑hosted, Apache‑2.0 licensed unified API for running multiple LLM agents like Codex, Claude, and Hermes with session, streaming, and error handling.
items.detail: The router implements the open Unified Harness Protocol, letting users keep their API keys and infrastructure while accessing diverse models through a single endpoint. It supports features such as file uploads, cancellation, and failure management.

items.title: MaaAssistantArknights/MaaAssistantArknights
items.summary: MaaAssistantArknights is a C++ tool that automates daily tasks in the game Arknights with a single click, supporting all client versions.
items.detail: The assistant streamlines routine gameplay actions, reducing manual effort for players. It is open‑source and targets the Chinese market, offering a convenient way to manage in‑game resources and events.

items.title: Panniantong/Agent-Reach
items.summary: Agent-Reach is a CLI tool that lets an AI agent browse and search major web platforms like Twitter, Reddit, YouTube, GitHub, Bilibili, and XiaoHongShu without requiring API keys.
items.detail: The tool aggregates public content from each service and presents it in a unified text interface, enabling downstream AI workflows to retrieve up‑to‑date information. It operates purely over publicly available endpoints, avoiding rate‑limited or paid APIs. Suitable for rapid prototyping of internet‑aware agents.

items.title: aseprite/aseprite
items.summary: Aseprite is a cross‑platform editor for creating animated pixel art and sprite sheets on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
items.detail: The application supports layers, onion‑skinning, and a timeline for frame‑by‑frame animation, making it popular among game developers. It is written in C++ and distributed under a proprietary license with a paid purchase model. Community extensions add scripting and custom export pipelines.

items.title: gitroomhq/postiz-app
items.summary: Postiz‑app is a social‑media scheduling platform that uses AI agents to automate content planning and posting.
items.detail: The service integrates with major social networks and offers features like optimal posting time suggestions, automated caption generation, and analytics dashboards. It markets itself as an "agentic" tool, implying AI‑driven decision making for scheduling. The product is currently in beta and available via a web interface.

items.title: Alishahryar1/free-claude-code
items.summary: free-claude-code provides free access to Claude Code, Codex, and six other LLM harnesses, offering over 1.3 billion free tokens across terminals, IDEs, and browsers.
items.detail: The project bundles multiple model back‑ends into a single CLI, supporting voice interaction and browser‑based sessions. It includes a ToS‑friendly wrapper called OpenClaw and works with VSCode, Pi, and other environments. Users can switch models on the fly without separate API keys.
